tasks.short: Build the monthly management pack: P&L per site, budget against actual, and a note on what moved.

today.trigger: Month close is signed off in AFAS (working day 5 to 7), or the Finance Director asks for an ad-hoc update.
steps: Export the trial balance and cost-centre figures from AFAS into the Excel pack template
Refresh Power BI finance pages and check they match the AFAS totals
Look up the drivers behind big variances (agency hours, fuel, overtime per site) in AFAS and agency invoices
Write the commentary per site and per cost group in Word or PowerPoint
Walk the Controller and Finance Director through the pack and fix their comments
drudgery: Copying the same exports into the same Excel tabs every month
Reconciling Power BI totals to AFAS by hand
Rewriting variance sentences that barely change month to month
today.time_sinks: Chasing the reason behind a variance across AFAS, agency portals and site managers' mail takes more time than the numbers themselves.

lenses.faster: The export, tie-out to AFAS and first-draft commentary run on their own; the accountant spends about half the old time checking explanations and adding what the numbers do not show.
lenses.autonomous: Close sign-off in AFAS starts a script that builds the pack from the AFAS extract, flags variances above threshold and drafts commentary; the accountant approves before it goes to the Finance Director.
lenses.ambitious: A weekly site-level cost flash for the three site managers (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo), who today only see figures a month late; demand would grow if it got cheaper, since agency and overtime cost move week to week.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting exports and retyping variance lines; the accountant wants more time on the conversations with site managers about why costs moved.
lenses.options: Two or three readings of a variance (volume, rate, timing) side by side help the Finance Director decide whether a cost overrun needs action or is just a cut-off effect.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from building the pack to setting variance thresholds and owning the explanation; the accountant gains the right to decide what is flagged to management, and the job gets more analytical.
reach: FP&A Analyst: monthly budget-against-actual commentary, needs driver-based forecasting basics
Controller: first review of the management pack, needs materiality judgement

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which variance is a real business problem and which is a booking artefact, and telling a site manager that in a way they accept.
tasks.pattern_why: The numbers and thresholds are fixed rules in software; only the commentary is messy text, which one model call drafts over checked figures.

in_practice.trigger: Month-close status set to closed in AFAS and the nightly extract refreshed.
steps: Script pulls trial balance and cost centres from the AFAS extract and ties totals to AFAS
Variances above the agreed threshold are listed per site with driver data (agency hours, fuel, overtime)
Model drafts commentary per variance, citing the source lines it used
Accountant edits and approves the pack, then sends it to the Finance Director
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves every commentary line and the tie-out before the pack is shared.
data_needed: AFAS trial balance and cost-centre extract
Budget per site and cost group
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint close folder: pack version, tie-out result and approved commentary per month.

evidence.claim: Accountants using AI closed 7.5 days faster in a field study of 79 firms.
Models beat licensed CPAs on month-end scenarios that reward detail and instruction following, but leave out client communication and tacit context.
Variance commentary over fixed figures is a standard single model-call task.

risks: Commentary states a plausible but wrong cause for a variance
Pack totals drift from AFAS if the extract fails silently overnight
Management stops asking questions because the text sounds confident
research_questions: How many commentary lines per month does the Controller change today, and would drafts cut that?
Does the nightly AFAS extract carry enough driver data (hours, kilometres) to explain site variances?
Would site managers use a weekly cost flash, and who would answer their follow-up questions?

tasks.short: Prepare the VAT return, ICP listing and corporate tax return from AFAS and make sure they are filed and paid on time.

today.trigger: VAT period end (monthly or quarterly), the yearly corporate tax deadline, or a provisional assessment from the Belastingdienst.
steps: Run the VAT report in AFAS and reconcile VAT accounts to the ledger
Check reverse-charge, intra-EU and import VAT postings and fix wrong VAT codes
Prepare the ICP declaration and check customer VAT numbers
Fill in the return in AFAS, have the Controller review it and file it
Schedule the payment in the Rabobank batch
drudgery: Hunting wrong VAT codes line by line
Reconciling VAT accounts to the return by hand each period
Checking foreign VAT numbers one at a time
today.time_sinks: Fixing miscoded purchase invoices, especially agency and foreign carrier invoices, takes most of the time before the return can be filled in.

lenses.faster: VAT code checks, reconciliation to the ledger and VAT-number validation run as scripts; the accountant reviews exceptions and the return, roughly 40% less time per period.
lenses.autonomous: Period end starts the checks over every VAT posting in AFAS; Jonas assists in the return form; the accountant approves and the Controller signs before filing.
lenses.ambitious: A VAT code check every week instead of at period end, so bookkeepers fix miscodings while the invoice is fresh; demand grows if cheaper, because errors found late cost more to fix.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss scanning lines for wrong VAT codes; the accountant wants more time on the tricky cross-border and reverse-charge cases.
lenses.options: Little here: the return has one right answer, though scenarios help when choosing between monthly and quarterly filing or planning provisional corporate tax payments.
lenses.altitude: The accountant writes and maintains the VAT coding rules and checks the bookkeepers work against, and decides which exceptions are fixed before filing; more expert, less clerical.
reach: Bookkeeper: VAT coding on purchase invoices, would need to own the coding rules in AFAS
Controller: first review of the VAT return, needs signing authority

tasks.human_edge: Judging unusual cross-border transactions and dealing with the Belastingdienst; the filer stays responsible for the return.
tasks.pattern_why: VAT code rules, account reconciliation and VAT-number checks can be written down and run without a model.

steps: Script checks every posting's VAT code against supplier, customer country and ledger rules
VAT accounts are reconciled to the draft return; differences listed
Customer VAT numbers checked for the ICP listing
Jonas in AFAS assists in completing the return; accountant reviews exceptions
Controller approves, accountant files and schedules payment
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant clears every exception and the Controller approves the return before filing.
data_needed: All VAT postings for the period
Supplier and customer master data with country and VAT number
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint tax folder: check results, exceptions cleared, filed return and approval.

evidence.claim: AFAS Jonas assists in income and corporate tax returns from 2022 and VAT (OB) from 2026; the user stays responsible for the check.
Tax estimates belong on the mandatory human review list.
Intra-EU and reverse-charge invoices are due within 10 days under ViDA; domestic application is open.

risks: A wrong coding rule repeats the same error across every return
Over-reliance on Jonas without checking the underlying ledger
No benchmark covers Dutch VAT, so tool accuracy is unproven
research_questions: What share of VAT corrections today come from a few repeatable miscodings (agency, foreign carriers)?
Does Jonas for VAT (OB) work on Noordhaven's Profit version and setup?
How long does the Controller's review take now, and would an exception list shorten it?

tasks.short: Review the balance sheet and P&L at close: check balances, movements and odd items before sign-off.

today.trigger: Month-end close, quarter end, or the annual audit.
steps: Export balances per account from AFAS and compare to last month and budget
Reconcile key accounts (bank, debtors, creditors, accruals, fixed assets, agency payables)
Investigate movements above threshold and ask bookkeepers or sites for explanations
Book correcting or adjusting entries
Document the review in the Excel close file
drudgery: Building the same flux analysis each month
Ticking off reconciliations that always match
Mailing for explanations of small movements
today.time_sinks: Explaining movements on accruals and agency payables, where the support sits in agency portals and mail threads.

lenses.faster: Flux analysis, standard reconciliations and the first explanation draft run automatically; the accountant reviews flagged accounts only, about half the old time.
lenses.autonomous: Close day 2 starts the flux and reconciliation run; matched accounts are marked done, others get a drafted explanation and proposed entry for the accountant to approve.
lenses.ambitious: A weekly balance sheet health check instead of monthly, so accrual and agency payable errors are caught before close; demand grows if cheaper, since it shortens days to close.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking reconciliations that always match; the accountant wants more time on the few accounts that really need judgement.
lenses.options: Drafting two treatments for a disputed accrual (book now or disclose) helps the Controller decide, but most reviews have one answer.
lenses.altitude: The accountant sets thresholds, reconciliation rules and the review checklist and decides which accounts are reviewed by hand; more expert work.
reach: Bookkeeper: bank and creditor reconciliations, needs to own matching rules
Controller: balance sheet sign-off for low-risk accounts, needs delegated authority

tasks.human_edge: Spotting the movement that makes no business sense and knowing who to ask; deciding on judgemental accruals and provisions.
tasks.pattern_why: Thresholds and reconciliations are rules; one model call drafts the explanation from the linked transactions, inside a fixed close workflow.

in_practice.trigger: Close day 2 in the close calendar, after subledgers are locked in AFAS.
steps: Script compares balances to prior month and budget and runs standard reconciliations
Accounts within tolerance are marked reconciled
Model drafts an explanation for each flagged movement from the underlying transactions
Accountant approves explanations and any proposed adjusting entry, which a person posts in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves every explanation and adjusting entry; nothing is posted without them.
in_practice.logs_to: Close file on SharePoint: reconciliation status, explanation and approver per account.

evidence.claim: Workday's Accounting Agent prepares entries and recommends schedules while teams stay responsible for review.
Multi-step reasoning across files causes over half of the top model's errors on accounting tasks.
A model can add an unnoticed assumption so the workpaper cannot be rebuilt.

risks: Explanations rest on an assumption nobody notices
Thresholds set too wide hide real errors
Audit trail incomplete if the drafted explanation is not linked to its sources
research_questions: Which accounts take most review time today, and are they rule-based or judgement-based?
Would the external auditor accept automated reconciliation evidence?
How often do flagged movements turn out to be real errors?

tasks.short: Write up findings from internal control checks and audit follow-up for the Controller and the external auditor.

today.trigger: An internal control test is finished, the auditor's management letter arrives, or a check on agency invoices finds problems.
steps: Collect test results and samples from Excel and AFAS
Describe each finding: what happened, the impact, the root cause
Agree the finding and actions with the process owner
Write the report in Word with recommendations and owners
Track follow-up until closed
drudgery: Turning test sheets into formal finding text
Formatting the report
Chasing status updates on open actions
today.time_sinks: Writing clear finding text and agreeing wording with process owners takes longer than the tests.

lenses.faster: The model drafts findings in a fixed format straight from test results; the accountant checks facts and wording, roughly 45% less time.
lenses.autonomous: A finished test run starts a draft finding per exception with evidence links; the accountant approves and sends it to the process owner.
lenses.ambitious: Short findings reports to each site manager after every agency invoice check, a group that today only hears about problems once a year; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss formatting findings; the accountant wants more time agreeing fixes with process owners.
lenses.options: Drafting a finding at two severity levels helps the Controller decide what goes to the auditor and what stays internal.
lenses.altitude: The accountant decides severity and which findings go to management, and spends the week on root causes rather than prose; more expert.
reach: Controller: first draft of the management letter response, needs knowledge of the auditor's expectations
Credit and Collections Officer: write-ups of debtor process findings, needs order-to-cash process knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Judging severity, getting a process owner to accept a finding, and being fair to the people named in it.
tasks.pattern_why: Test results are structured; one model call turns them into finding text that the accountant checks against the evidence.

in_practice.trigger: Control test results saved to the SharePoint audit folder.
steps: Exceptions from the test file are read with their evidence links
Model drafts each finding: condition, criterion, impact, proposed action
Accountant checks facts and severity and edits the text
Approved findings go to process owners and into the action tracker
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves each finding and its severity before anyone outside Finance sees it.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint findings register with draft, approved version, owner and due date.

evidence.claim: Writing structured findings from test results is a routine drafting task for current models.
Models still fail judgement-heavy accounting tasks; judgement, not retrieval, is the bottleneck.

risks: Findings name employees, so AVG/GDPR applies to the drafts and logs
Drafted text overstates or understates severity
Process owners push back on machine-written findings
research_questions: How many findings per year does the team write, and how long does each take?
Does the works council need to be informed if findings about named staff are drafted by AI?
Would the external auditor rely on findings drafted this way?

tasks.short: Work out the company's corporate tax position: fiscal depreciation, provisions, interest limits and deferred tax.

today.trigger: Year-end, the provisional corporate tax assessment, or a big transaction (new warehouse, truck lease, asset sale).
steps: Pull the commercial result and fixed asset register from AFAS
Compute fiscal versus commercial differences (depreciation of buildings, trucks, forklifts; provisions)
Check interest deduction limits and lease treatment
Compute current and deferred tax in Excel
Agree the position with the Controller and the tax adviser
drudgery: Rebuilding the fiscal depreciation schedule each year
Copying asset data into the tax workbook
today.time_sinks: Reconciling the fiscal and commercial asset registers and documenting each choice for the tax adviser.

lenses.faster: Asset data, fiscal depreciation and the deferred tax roll-forward are computed in a fixed workbook; the accountant reviews and makes the judgement calls, saving about 30%.
lenses.autonomous: Year-end triggers the computation from AFAS; Jonas assists in the corporate tax return; every estimate is approved by the accountant and the Controller.
lenses.ambitious: Tax impact scenarios for each capital decision (new warehouse, electric trucks, lease or buy) for the Finance Director, which today happen rarely; demand grows if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the depreciation schedule; the accountant wants more time on tax planning choices.
lenses.options: Scenarios matter here: lease versus buy, depreciation choices and investment allowances change the decision, not just the effort.
lenses.altitude: The accountant brings tax scenarios to investment decisions and owns the tax position file; the job becomes more expert.
reach: FP&A Analyst: tax lines in the forecast, needs forecast model skills
Controller: deferred tax note in the annual accounts, needs Dutch GAAP disclosure knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Tax estimates and positions need human judgement and sign-off; dealing with the tax adviser and the Belastingdienst stays human.
tasks.pattern_why: The work turns on judgement about positions and estimates; the accountant leads and the tool computes and checks.

in_practice.trigger: Year-end close or a capital decision request from the Finance Director.
steps: Workbook pulls the asset register and result from AFAS
Fiscal depreciation, interest limit and deferred tax are computed
Accountant asks the assistant for scenarios and checks each against the rules
Position memo agreed with the Controller and tax adviser
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Controller approve every estimate and position before booking or filing.
in_practice.logs_to: Tax position file on SharePoint with assumptions, scenarios and sign-off.

evidence.claim: AFAS Jonas assists in corporate tax returns; the user remains responsible for the check.
Tax estimates belong on the mandatory human review list.
No benchmark covers Dutch tax work.

risks: Wrong assumption in a scenario changes an investment decision
Model applies non-Dutch tax rules
Position documentation too thin for the tax adviser or audit
research_questions: How many capital decisions a year would benefit from tax scenarios?
How much of the tax adviser's fee goes on data preparation the accountant could do?
Does Jonas cover the fiscal versus commercial asset differences Noordhaven has?

tasks.short: Check AFAS and the agency and bank links for weak controls: rights, duties, master data changes. Recommend fixes.

today.trigger: Yearly control review, an auditor's IT finding, a new AFAS module, or a payment incident.
steps: Export user roles and authorisations from AFAS
Check segregation of duties (creditor master data versus payment batches)
Sample IBAN and supplier changes and check approvals
Review interfaces with agency portals and Rabobank for gaps
Write recommendations and agree them with the Controller and IT
drudgery: Cross-matching role exports in Excel
Sampling master data changes by hand
today.time_sinks: Matching authorisation exports against the duties matrix and following up each odd case with IT.

lenses.faster: Duty conflicts, IBAN changes and odd master data edits are tested over every record instead of a sample; the accountant reviews hits and writes recommendations, saving about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly job tests every AFAS change for duty conflicts and unapproved IBAN changes and raises exceptions; the accountant handles the exceptions.
lenses.ambitious: Continuous payment fraud checks on every Rabobank batch before release, a decision made each run instead of once a year; demand grows as fraud attempts increase.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss cross-matching role exports in Excel; the accountant wants more time designing better controls with IT.
lenses.options: Several control designs side by side (block, approve, monitor) help the Controller weigh friction against risk.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs and owns the control tests and decides which exceptions are escalated; the job becomes more expert and closer to IT audit.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: AFAS authorisation reviews on HR modules, needs AFAS role model knowledge
Bookkeeper: supplier master data checks, needs to follow the test rules

tasks.human_edge: Judging which control fits how people really work in the warehouses and offices, and persuading owners to change process.
tasks.pattern_why: Duty conflicts, IBAN change approvals and duplicate checks are rules that run over every record without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly after the AFAS extract, and before each Rabobank payment batch is released.
steps: Script tests roles against the segregation-of-duties matrix
Every IBAN and supplier change is checked for a second approver
Payment batch lines are checked for duplicates and changed bank details
Exceptions go to the accountant's queue; recommendations written by hand
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant reviews each exception; payment batches with a hit are held until cleared.
data_needed: AFAS user roles and audit log
in_practice.logs_to: Control log on SharePoint and a Power BI exception page.

evidence.claim: Rule-based tests over every transaction (duplicates, segregation of duties, IBAN changes) suit deterministic software at high autonomy.

risks: AFAS audit log access limited or incomplete
Too many false positives so exceptions are ignored
Holding payment batches delays agency payments
research_questions: Does the AFAS extract include the audit log of master data changes?
How many IBAN changes happen per month and how many lack a second approver?
Would the auditor reduce sample testing if full-population tests run?

tasks.short: Prepare the annual accounts under Dutch GAAP, support the audit and file with KVK via SBR.

today.trigger: Financial year end; audit planning with the external auditor.
steps: Close the year in AFAS and build the lead schedules
Draft the balance sheet, P&L and notes in Word and Excel
Tie every note to the ledger and prepare the audit file
Process audit adjustments and update the accounts
File the accounts with KVK via SBR
drudgery: Rolling forward last year's notes
Tying out each number in the notes by hand
Answering repeated auditor data requests
today.time_sinks: Tie-out of notes to the ledger and the back-and-forth with the auditor on supporting files.

lenses.faster: Lead schedules and note roll-forwards are drafted and tied to AFAS automatically; the accountant checks and handles judgement areas, about 35% less time.
lenses.autonomous: Year-end close triggers draft schedules and notes with a tie-out check; nothing goes to the auditor until the accountant approves.
lenses.ambitious: Quarterly mini-accounts for the Finance Director and the bank, so audit adjustments surface during the year; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss manual tie-outs; the accountant wants more time on the judgement areas and the auditor discussion.
lenses.options: Little: the accounts have one answer, though drafting alternative note wording for provisions helps the Controller choose.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the tie-out rules and the audit file and decides what goes to the auditor; fewer audit adjustments and a more expert role.
reach: Controller: first draft of the annual report notes, needs Dutch GAAP (Titel 9 BW2) depth
FP&A Analyst: year-end bridge to the budget

tasks.human_edge: Judgement on provisions, valuation and disclosure, and the relationship with the external auditor.
tasks.pattern_why: Numbers come from AFAS by rule; one model call rolls forward note text, and a tie-out gate checks every figure.

steps: Script builds lead schedules from AFAS
Model rolls forward last year's notes with this year's figures
Tie-out checks every number in the notes against the ledger
Accountant reviews, Controller approves, accountant files via SBR
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Controller approve the accounts; tie-out must pass before release.
in_practice.logs_to: Audit file on SharePoint with tie-out results and approvals.

evidence.claim: Large companies file accounts with KVK via SBR from FY2025 and AFAS cannot file this for them.
On 160 US GAAP tasks the leading model meets 61.8% of criteria; judgement is the bottleneck.
No benchmark covers Dutch GAAP or a statutory audit file.

risks: Note text applies US GAAP habits to Dutch GAAP
A figure passes the tie-out but the disclosure is wrong
Auditor reliance unclear on AI-drafted notes
research_questions: How many hours does the tie-out take today and how many audit adjustments come from it?
Will the external auditor accept the automated tie-out evidence?
Which SBR filing tool will Noordhaven use since AFAS cannot file?

tasks.short: Check that transactions are recorded right and comply, for example agency invoices, and ask staff how it really works.

today.trigger: Audit planning, a compliance check (agency invoices, G-account payments), or a signal from bookkeepers.
steps: Select records to examine in AFAS and agency portals
Compare hours, rates and invoices against orders and contracts
Interview warehouse planners and site staff about how goods and hours are recorded
Note gaps and compliance issues
Agree corrections with the owners
drudgery: Matching agency hours to invoices by hand
Gathering documents before interviews
today.time_sinks: Pulling records from three agency portals into one view before any checking can start.

lenses.faster: Matching agency hours, rates and invoices runs over every line and an interview pack is prepared; the interviews and judgement stay, saving about 25%.
lenses.autonomous: Each agency invoice run triggers the match; exceptions land with the accountant, who decides what to examine and whom to interview.
lenses.ambitious: Checks of flex worker pay against the CAO rates for every agency invoice, a group whose pay is rarely checked today; demand grows in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying portal data into Excel; the accountant wants more time on the floor understanding how work is recorded.
lenses.options: Little: the work is fact-finding, not choosing between drafts.
lenses.altitude: The accountant spends the week on interviews and fixes instead of matching data, and decides where to look; more expert and more visible.
reach: Bookkeeper: agency invoice matching, needs the match rules
Payroll Specialist: CAO rate checks for flex workers, needs CAO knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Interviewing staff, reading what is not written down and building trust on the sites.
tasks.pattern_why: The accountant leads the examination and interviews; the tool prepares data and flags gaps.

in_practice.trigger: Agency invoices received or a compliance check scheduled.
steps: Match hours, rates and invoices across agency portals and AFAS
Flag rate, hour and CAO mismatches
Prepare an interview pack with the exceptions
Accountant interviews staff and records conclusions
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant decides on every conclusion and correction; interviews stay human.
in_practice.logs_to: Compliance file on SharePoint with matches, exceptions and interview notes.

evidence.claim: Models leave out asking the right questions and building tacit context.

risks: Interview notes contain personal data under AVG/GDPR
Agency portal exports differ in format and break matching
Staff see checks as distrust; works council may want to be informed
research_questions: Can all three agency portals export hours and invoices in a usable format?
How much overbilling or rate error is found today per year?
Does the works council need to agree to checks that touch flex worker hours?

role.altitude: From building reports, returns and reconciliations by hand to owning the rules, thresholds, tie-outs and control tests that check every entry, with the right to decide what is flagged, held or escalated.
reach: Bookkeeper: VAT coding and agency invoice matching rules
Controller: first review of management pack and low-risk balance sheet sign-off
FP&A Analyst: variance commentary and tax lines in the forecast
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: AFAS authorisation reviews
role.ceiling_note: Judgement on estimates, tax positions, Dutch GAAP disclosure and audit relationships stays human, and no benchmark covers Dutch GAAP or VAT; realistic savings are 25 to 50% per task, about a third of the role's hours.
skills_to_grow: Writing testable rules and checks in Python or SQL over the AFAS extract
Control design and IT audit basics
Reviewing AI drafts for hidden assumptions
Tax scenario modelling for capital decisions
role.ambitious_version: Run continuous controls and a weekly site cost flash for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, so the month closes in fewer days with fewer audit adjustments and site managers act on costs weekly.
